claims.text: Under sustained elevated-temperature loading, progressive plastic deformation is driven by gradual formation of partial amorphous gradient zones.
Partial amorphous gradient zones form at coherent FCC/BCC multilayer interfaces.
Amorphous gradient zones absorb or annihilate incoming dislocations.
The gradient zones redistribute stress and reduce interfacial stress concentrations.
Formation of the gradient zones enables continuous creep deformation.
Formation of the gradient zones prevents premature catastrophic failure.
The proposed starting material is a nanoscale coating of alternating coherent FCC and BCC high-entropy-alloy layers with minimal preexisting amorphous character.
Temperatures in the 1000–1400 K range can enable creep processes under an applied load.
The proposed elevated-temperature loading can retain the nanoscale multilayer architecture.
Restricting stepwise strain-rate increases to no more than tenfold will avoid over-softening and preserve multilayer integrity.
Dislocation nucleation preferentially occurs in the FCC regions because they have lower Peierls barriers.
The adjacent BCC layers offer greater resistance to dislocation-mediated deformation than the FCC layers.
Dislocation pile-ups at FCC/BCC interfaces trigger local structural transitions that initiate partial amorphization.
Interfacial amorphous regions accommodate plastic strain through combined dislocation activity and localized structural reordering.
The extent of amorphous or semi-amorphous interfacial zones will progressively increase with creep time.
Dislocation density will be lower near or within the amorphous interfacial zones than in the surrounding crystalline matrix.
Growth of the amorphous interfacial zones will correlate with acceleration of the creep rate.
Higher temperature increases atomic mobility, accelerates creep, and lowers creep resistance.
The starting baseline has a uniform dislocation distribution and lacks significant amorphous regions.
The relative contributions of dislocation climb and localized diffusion to interfacial amorphization are not quantified.

contradictions.description: The intervention specifies constant sustained-load creep, whereas the conditions specify a controlled strain rate with stepwise increases. These are different loading-control modes and are not reconciled.
